newsitem.title: UK: East Anglia grain farmers may face water curbs.
newsitem.headline: East Anglia grain farmers may face water curbs.

text.p: Farmers in parts of East Anglia, one of the most important grain growing areas of Britain, are likely to face restrictions on the use of water for irrigation.
"It's probable, rather than possible, that restrictions will be widespread," a regional spokesman for the Environment Agency, which controls the abstraction of water by farmers, told Reuters.
There are already some voluntary restrictions, he said.
Rainfall in the region over the last two years has been the lowest on record, he said, leaving groundwater levels precariously low.
East Anglia relies on winter rainfall to replenish its stock of groundwater, he said. Half of the water in its rivers comes from that source.

Demand from farmers for water for irrigation depends on the weather over the summer. "If it's normal there'll be a lot of demand. If it rains throughout the summer there shouldn't be too much of a problem," he said.
On the basis of current water stocks and weather in previous years the agency has looked at where problems are possible, he said.
Suffolk and Essex in particular are likely to have problems, he said. "Norfolk appears to be better off."
Many places in Suffolk had reached the lowest recorded water levels for this time of year.
The procedure for controlling water usage started with a process of consultation with farmers' groups and the ministry of agriculture, which was already under way.

Restrictions, if necessary, would be issued on a phased basis, with total bans on abstraction as the most dramatic action which could be taken. The agency would try to avoid total bans, but could not rule them out, the spokesman said.
In parts of Suffolk some licence holders had already been asked to make savings in the volume of water they use.
